title: Bridging Gaps in Simulation Analysis through a General Purpose, Bidirectional Steering Interface with Ascent
problem: Traditional in situ analysis and visualization workflows rely on automated triggers that cannot respond to interactive user input, limiting scientists' ability to make adjustments during simulation execution. This lack of interactive control requires costly cold restarts to modify simulation parameters or explore alternative scenarios.
motivation: Interactive human-in-the-loop steering of simulations can significantly improve scientific productivity by eliminating restart overhead and accelerating setup, troubleshooting, and parameter exploration.
method: The paper introduces a bridge that enables interactive steering of running simulations by letting scientists pause between timesteps, adjust simulation parameters (like model inputs) or analysis settings, and resume without cold restarts. This bridge works with any in situ analysis system (the tools that examine simulations as they run), with Ascent as a reference implementation. Rather than relying on automated, hands-off analysis, the interface puts scientists in real-time control, letting them respond to emerging results immediately.
key_novelty: An interactive steering interface that's library-agnostic (compatible with any in situ analysis tool) and lets scientists pause running simulations to adjust parameters in real time, without restart overhead.
contributions: General-purpose interface design for interactive simulation steering agnostic to in situ visualization libraries
Reference implementation integrated with Ascent for large-scale simulations
Demonstration that interactive steering eliminates cold restart overhead
Two use cases showing productivity improvements through pause-and-adjust workflows

metrics.other: Eliminated cold restart overhead, improved setup and troubleshooting time

primary_theme: Interactive steering interface for HPC simulations
